newsitem.title: USA: Brady bonds thinly mixed, players await Fed's move.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds thinly mixed, players await Fed's move.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices closed thinly mixed Monday, with Russia debt weakening further as traders waited for Federal Reserve policy makers to meet Tuesday.
"We have low volume position type of squaring," said one trader. "People are mainly focused on tommorow's meeting."

The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the policy setting arm of the Federal Reserve, meets Tuesday. The market remained split on the outcome of the meeting, with a slim majority of economists polled by Reuters expecting a hike of a 25 basis points in official U.S. interest rates.
"The market's a little bit better on most of the Latin credits than where we went out on Friday," another trader said. "Argentina has probably been the best performer."
Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR were quoted up 3/8 at 82-1/2 following last week's volatile session, traders said.
"The bond has had a pretty decent correction already," said one trader. "Between Wednesday and Friday, of last week the bonds traded as high as 85 and as low as 82."
In other issues, Argentina PARs AR4C23=RR were quoted unchanged at 56-5/8, traders said.
Buying interest picked up toward the end ot the day, traders said. "We saw a nice rebound in the (Treasury) bond...that's helped us out a lot," said one trader.
"There was a little more willingness to buy towards the end of the day with players seeming a bit more comfortable going into the (FOMC) meeting long than short," the trader added.
Meanwhile, uncertainty over President Boris Yeltsin's health condition continues to mount, traders said.
Russian shares and bonds fell on Monday following news that a heart operation on the 65-year old leader may be delayed for up to two months or abandoned altogether.
"We've seen weakeness in Russia bonds all day long mainly because of Yeltsin's condition," said one trader. "The Vnesh has suffered a five point loss since last Thursday."

Russian US$ Vnesh was better bid at 65-1/4 in New York, off from the day's lows of 64-3/8 during the London trading session. However, sharply lower than last Thursday when the issue traded above 70, traders said.
In other issues, Mexican Pars MX625L19=RR lost 1/4 to trade at 68-3/8 while Mexican UMS-26 MXUMS=RR also fell 1/4 at 98-3/8, traders added.
Brazilian C bonds BR8D14=RR traded up 1/4 at 68-3/4, traders said.
In the government market, the 30-year Treasury bond up 8/32 at 96-19/32 to yield 7.02 percent.
